mirror_virtual_camera — DRIVE decide op

• Data kinds: any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.mirror_virtual_camera(cam_pose, mirror_plane) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivedecide; drivedecide.mirror_virtual_camera(cam_pose, mirror_plane) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("mirror_virtual_camera"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

A virtual camera that captures the image seen in a plane mirror.

cam_pose is the world→camera 4×4 (convention of render3d.look_at: X_cam = P X, −Z forward). mirror_plane is (n_x, n_y, n_z, d) (n·X = d).

Return value (dict):

• reflection: the reflection S (mirror_reflection_matrix).

• pose_mirrored = P·S: rendering the real scene with this gives exactly the image the real camera sees through the mirror (identical down to pixel positions). The determinant of the rotation part is −1 (a left-right reversed coordinate system; depending on the renderer, front/back face determination is inverted).

• pose = F·P·S, F = diag(−1, 1, 1, 1): an ordinary right-handed camera (determinant +1) = the virtual camera behind the mirror. An image taken with it is the left-right flip of the image in the mirror (in pixels u' = 2c_x − u). Use this when treating a rear-view mirror as "a rear-facing camera" (flip left-right to get back the image the driver sees).

• eye: position of the virtual camera S(C) (C = position of the real camera). eye_real: C.

• flip: "x" (flipping x of the pose image gives the mirror image).

Closed form: S(X) = X − 2(n·X − d)n. The image of a point Q seen in the mirror is at S(Q) (on the far side of the mirror, at the same distance from the mirror surface). Gate (test): solve numerically for the point M on the mirror that satisfies angle of incidence = angle of reflection (Fermat's shortest path), and check that C + (|CM| + |MQ|)·unit(M − C) coincides with S(Q).
